author: larsbrinkhoff
body:
There is a PDP-11 Chaosnet router/terminal concentrator called NSWIT, or New Switch.  It's similar to MINITS, but older.  NSWIT may have started at MIT, but was later mainly in use at the S-1 project at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (often called LLL).  There may also be some connection to the Plasma Physics TV system, see #1837.  NSWIT has support for both the "MIT keyboard" (probably Space Cadet) and SAIL keyboards.

I believe the MIT copy was in the CHSNCP directory.  We have some scraps of files from there, e.g. NSWIT 106 and 276.

We do have a full set of files from SAIL:
- \[SW,CBF] - plain NSWIT by @cbf66 
- \[GRN,CBF] - with Grinnell support
- \[NCP,CBF] - with Arpanet NCP support
- \[1,EAK] - another copy by @eak 

I tested assembing NSWIT.PAL\[SW,CBF] and that went fine, both with ITS' PALX, and the one in \[1,EAK].

I believe NSWIT was often run on an LSI-11, and was probably started from RT-11.

author: bhearsum
body:
This (fairly hefty) pull request adds a new scriptworker: landoscript. This new scriptworker will be replacing treescript when writes to hg.mozilla.org for Gecko repositories cease to happen.

Because it ultimately fulfills the same use cases as treescript, I've chosen to keep the payload as similar as possible. There are some necessary changes (mostly around using lando repository names instead of references to hg.mozilla.org repositories). I've also removed support for some things that are not used (eg: `ignore_closed_tree` and `dontbuild` are either not present for most actions, or always have the same value).

Some notes on the tests included here:
* Most of the success tests have payloads taken directly from real world treescript tasks (with some small tweaks, per the above note). I fished around and tried to find all variations of these tasks that exist (most notably for `merge_day` and `version_bump` tasks, which are often slightly different depending on which repository they are running from).
* The approach I've taken to testing here is the same as what I've been attempting to do for signingscript in https://github.com/mozilla-releng/scriptworker-scripts/pull/1097: execute tests by running `async_main`, rather than deeply unit testing individual components. This does end up making the tests notable bigger, which can be intimidating, but I've found that once written they need little to no touching, and has made refactoring as I go along significantly easier. There is probably an argument to be made that certain helper pure functions (like `diff_contents`) could do with some separate unit testing - but I've not gone to that length yet.
* I'm not terribly happy with how the responses for the github client are set-up. Because the GraphQL API uses a single endpoint for all requests, and I'm simply returning responses in a fixed order, the ordering of the `aioresponses` calls is important. In an ideal world we would be able to key responses off of parts of the requests, but I haven't had time to make this happen.

At the time of writing I have not yet been able to test it in a dev environment - I've merely been working off of the spec at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xYp6v4YLLHsX7zFkYoygDyvIUPzujxeMW7W4qte0o/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.c29tth48xps4. Seeing as this is completely unused so far, I'm hoping to get what's here merged, and then follow up with more targeted pull requests as I fix issues that I encounter when testing in the real world.

## What
Fix https://issues.redhat.com/browse/THREESCALE-9510

## Verification steps
* Checkout this branch and build a new runtime image
```
make runtime-image IMAGE_NAME=apicast-test
```
* Move into dev-environment
```
cd dev-environments/keycloak-env
```
* Edit `apicast-config.json` as follow
```diff
diff --git a/dev-environments/keycloak-env/apicast-config.json b/dev-environments/keycloak-env/apicast-config.json
index 071296cd..62fb24f5 100644
--- a/dev-environments/keycloak-env/apicast-config.json
+++ b/dev-environments/keycloak-env/apicast-config.json
@@ -90,6 +90,20 @@
               "auth_type": "use_3scale_oidc_issuer_endpoint"
             }
           },
+          {
+            "name": "apicast.policy.jwt_claim_check",
+            "configuration": {
+              "rules" : [{
+                  "operations": [
+                    {"op": "==", "jwt_claim": "{{jwt.realm_access.roles| first}}", "jwt_claim_type": "liquid", "value": "{{original_request.query | split: \"role=\" | last}}", "value_type": "liquid"}
+                  ],
+                  "combine_op": "and",
+                  "methods": ["GET"],
+                  "resource": "/"
+              }],
+              "enable_extended_context": true
+            }
+          },
           {
             "name": "apicast",
             "version": "builtin",
```
* Start gateway and seed keycloak data
```
make gateway IMAGE_NAME=apicast-test
make keycloak-data
```
* Retrieve access token
```
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(make token)
```
* Send a request and you should receive `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`
```
curl -v --resolve stg.example.com:8080:127.0.0.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" "http://stg.example.com:8080/?role=default-roles-basic"
```
* Now send another request with query `role=default-roles-basic3`
```
curl -v --resolve stg.example.com:8080:127.0.0.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" "http://stg.example.com:8080/?role=default-roles-basic3"
```
*  `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` should be returned

author: jondotsoy
body:
## Changes

This pull request introduces the following key changes:

1. **Add HTTP2 Listener**: A new `HTTP2Lister` class has been added that creates an HTTP2 server and integrates it with the existing `HTTPRouter` class. This allows the application to serve HTTP2 requests in addition to HTTP1.1 requests.
2. **Centralize Executable Paths**: New export variables have been added to provide the paths for various configuration and listener files, improving maintainability and flexibility.
3. **Improve Server Script Generation**: The server script generation has been simplified by using pre-defined executable paths, and an optional `withHttp2Listener` parameter has been added to the `makeServerScript` function.
4. **Add Support for HTTP2 and 404 Handling**: The `serve` command now supports running the server with HTTP2, and 404 errors are handled gracefully when the requested resource is not found.
5. **Add Support for Various Config File Formats**: The application now supports loading configuration files in YAML, JSON, TOML, and TypeScript formats, providing more flexibility and extensibility.
6. **Deprecate `getHTTPListenerMiddlewares` Method**: The `getHTTPListenerMiddlewares` method in the `Configs` class has been deprecated and replaced with a new `httpListenerMiddlewares` getter.
7. **Add Server Configs and HTTP2 Secure Context Options**: A new `ServerConfigs` class has been added to the `configs` module, and a new `http2SecureContextOptionsKey` property has been added to the `Configs` class.
8. **Add Support for SSL Configuration in HTTP2 Listener**: The `HTTP2Lister` class has been updated to support SSL configuration, allowing the application to use SSL/TLS for the HTTP/2 server.
9. **Add Support for Non-Secure HTTP2 Server**: The `HTTPRouter` class now supports creating both secure and non-secure HTTP2 servers.
10. **Add Support for Server Configs in HTTP Router**: The `HTTPRouter` class now reads server configuration options from the provided `configs` object, allowing the use of the configured port and hostname.
11. **Add Support for HTTPS in HTTP Listener**: The `HTTPLister` class now supports HTTPS, allowing the application to use both HTTP and HTTPS protocols.
12. **Update Auth Integration Tests**: The URL path used in the auth integration tests has been updated to use the correct relative path.
13. **Update Bun and Node.js Versions**: The project dependencies have been updated to use the latest stable versions of Bun (1.2.2) and Node.js (23.7.0).
14. **Implement Initial Port and Find Next Port**: The `http-router` module now uses the `INITIAL_PORT` constant and the `findNextPort` utility function to ensure a consistent starting point for the port selection process.
15. **Add Logging to Auth Integration Tests**: Console.log statements have been added to the auth integration tests to help with debugging and understanding the test environment.

These changes improve the functionality, maintainability, and flexibility of the application, particularly in the areas of HTTP/2 support, configuration handling, and server setup.

Parity, replaces Warden completely. Fixes #5540, fixes #4405

Usual process with new system for each ability. There's a new aura system for giving an outline to something, for the future and now used for fruits, steelcrest, and valkyrie. author: dhgudtmxhs
body:
### **`STEP 16`**

- 서비스의 규모가 확장되어 MSA의 형태로 각 도메인별로 배포단위를 분리해야한다면 그 분리에 따른 트랜잭션 처리의 한계와 해결방안에 대한 서비스 설계 문서 작성
- 실시간 주문을 데이터 플랫폼에 전달(mock API 호출)하는 로직을 기존 로직에 영향을 주지 않도록 개선

## 학습 내용

<details>
<summary>MSA 형태로 도메인 배포단위 분리 및 트랜잭션 처리 설계</summary>


## 1. 개요
기존의 단일 서버/단일 DB 기반 모놀리식 아키텍처 시스템을 MSA(Microservices Architecture) 환경으로 전환하여  
도메인별로 배포단위를 분리할 때, 발생하는 트랜잭션 처리 한계와 이를 해결하기 위한 방안을 세운다.


## 2. 기존 시스템 분석

### 2-1. 환경 및 구현 기술
- **시스템 환경**
  - 단일 서버, 단일 DB (모놀리식 아키텍처)
  - Docker 컨테이너를 통한 MySQL, Redis 운영
  - Docker 기반 테스트 환경 활용

- **트랜잭션 및 동시성 제어 기술**
  - **Redis 캐싱 및 저장:**   주문 처리, 사용자, 상품 데이터의 캐싱 및 별도 Redis DB 저장을 통해 성능 최적화
  - **분산 락**: 여러 인스턴스 간 동기화 
  - **DB 비관적 락**: 단일 DB 내 동시성 제어 (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`)

### 2-2 트랜잭션 처리 방식
- **ACID 트랜잭션:** 단일 DB 환경 내 `@Transactional` 을 통한 원자적 처리
- **추가 동기화:** Redis 캐싱 및 락 기법을 활용하여 데이터 정합성 유지

### 2-3 주요 도메인 및 비즈니스 로직
- **User:** 사용자 관리, 조회
- **Point:** 포인트 관리, 조회, 사용, 차감
- **Coupon:** 쿠폰과 사용자쿠폰(UserCoupon) 관리, 조회, 선착순 발급, 사용
- **Product:** 상품 관리, 조회
- **Order:** 주문 관리, 주문 처리, 주문 항목(OrderItem) 관리
- **Payment:** 결제 처리, 데이터 플랫폼 전송 (Mock)

## 3. 모놀리식 아키텍처 vs MSA

### 3-1. 모놀리식 아키텍처
- **특징**
  - **단일 배포 단위:**  모든 기능이 하나의 애플리케이션에 포함되어 배포 및 업데이트 시 전체 시스템을 함께 반영
  - **내부 통신:**  모듈 간 호출이 로컬 함수 호출처럼 빠르게 이루어짐
  - **개발 및 테스트 용이성:**  일관된 관리와 단순한 초기 환경 구축이 가능
- **단점**
  - **확장성 제한:** 일부 기능만 독립적으로 확장하기 어려움
  - **유지보수 복잡성:** 코드베이스가 커짐에 따라 모듈 간 의존성이 증가, 변경 시 영향 범위 확대
  - **기술 도입 제약:** 전체 시스템에 동일한 기술 스택 적용 필요

### 3-2. MSA(분산 시스템)의 필요성 및 특징
- **필요성**
  - **확장성:** 서비스별 독립 확장을 통해 부하 분산으로 트래픽 대응이 가능
  - **신뢰성 및 장애 격리:** 특정 서비스 장애가 전체 시스템에 미치는 영향을 최소화
  - **성능 최적화:** 다중 서버를 통한 병렬 처리 및 특정 기능 최적화 가능
  - **유연한 유지보수:** 서비스 단위 변경 및 배포로 업데이트 리스크 감소

- **MSA 주요 특징**
  - **독립적인 확장성:** 각 서비스가 개별적으로 확장 가능
  - **도메인 기반 유지보수:** 각 도메인을 독립 서비스로 관리하여 빠른 개선 및 배포 가능
  - **장애 격리:** 서비스 단위 장애 발생 시 전체 시스템에 미치는 영향 최소화
  - **독립 배포 및 운영:** 서비스별로 기술 스택 선택 및 팀 운영 분리 가능
  - **서비스 간 통신:** REST, gRPC, 메시지 큐(Kafka, RabbitMQ) 및 서킷 브레이커 패턴 적용

## 4. MSA 환경 전환 시 고려 사항

### 4-1. 기존 트랜잭션 처리 (모놀리식)
- **단일 DB 내 ACID 보장**
  - `@Transactional` 을 활용하여 모든 작업(INSERT, UPDATE 등)이 원자적으로 처리됨
- **동시성 제어를 위한 락 사용**
  - **비관적 락 (Pessimistic Lock):** `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` 를 활용
  - **분산 락 (Redis 기반):** Redisson 등을 이용해 락을 적용, 단일 DB 환경에서는 일관되게 동작

### 4-2. 도메인 개별 분리 후 트랜잭션 처리 (MSA)
- **트랜잭션 한계**
  - 각 서비스가 개별 DB를 사용하므로, 단일 트랜잭션으로 묶기 어려움
  - 네트워크나 서비스 장애 발생 시 ACID 보장에 한계
  - 기존의 비관적 락은 각 DB에만 적용되어 전역 동시성 제어에 한계
  - Redis 기반 분산 락은 가능하지만, 트랜잭션과 별도로 관리해야 함

## 5. 분산 트랜잭션 해결 방안

### 5-1. Redis 기반 분산 락 유지, DB 락 대체
- MSA 환경에서 각 서비스가 독립적인 DB를 사용하므로, 전역 동시성 제어를 위해 기존의 DB 비관적 락을 분산 락으로 대체
- Redis를 공통 리소스로 활용하여 여러 서비스 간에 일관된 동시성 제어 구현
- 네트워크 장애 대비를 위해 Redis Sentinel 또는 Cluster 구성 필요
- 트랜잭션과 락은 별도 관리되므로 TTL 설정 및 보상 트랜잭션 설계가 필요

### 5-2. 2PC (Two-Phase Commit)

- 2PC는 **분산 환경에서 여러 서비스 또는 DB가 하나의 논리적 트랜잭션을 일관되게 처리**하기 위한 프로토콜이다.
  1. **준비 단계(Prepare Phase)**  
     - **코디네이터:** 트랜잭션을 시작하고 참여 서비스(혹은 DB)에 준비 요청을 보낸다.
     - **참여 서비스:** 각 서비스는 로컬 트랜잭션을 실행하고, 성공 여부를 코디네이터에게 응답한다.
  2. **커밋 단계(Commit Phase)**  
     - **코디네이터:** 모든 참여 서비스가 준비를 완료했다는 응답을 받으면, 커밋 메시지를 전파한다.  
     - **참여 서비스:** 커밋 메시지를 수신하면 로컬 트랜잭션을 확정(commit)하고, 실패한 경우에는 롤백(rollback)한다.
  
- **장점:** 모든 참여자가 동일한 트랜잭션 결과(커밋 또는 롤백)를 보장받기 때문에 데이터 일관성이 유지된다.
  
- **단점 및 한계**  
  - **성능 저하:** 두 단계에 걸쳐 네트워크 왕복 시간이 발생하여 응답 속도가 느려질 수 있다.  
  - **블로킹 문제:** 한 참여 서비스가 응답을 지연시키거나 장애가 발생하면 전체 트랜잭션이 멈출 위험이 있다.  
  - **단일 실패 지점:** 코디네이터의 장애나 네트워크 문제로 인해 전체 트랜잭션이 중단될 수 있다.  
  - **확장성 제한:** 많은 서비스가 참여하면 시스템 전체의 응답 시간에 영향을 줄 수 있어 MSA 환경에서는 부담이 될 수 있다.

### 5-3. SAGA 패턴

- SAGA 패턴은 **분산 환경에서 트랜잭션을 개별 서비스의 로컬 트랜잭션 단위로 나누어 처리하는 방식**이다. 

- **트랜잭션 처리 방식**  
  - 각 서비스의 로컬 트랜잭션은 개별적으로 **커밋(commit)된 후 다음 서비스로 전파**된다.
  - 중간에 실패가 발생하면, **이전 단계에서 수행된 작업을 되돌리는 보상 트랜잭션(compensating transaction)을 실행**한다.

- **보장되는 일관성**  
  - SAGA 패턴은 **즉각적인 강한 일관성(Strong Consistency)** 을 제공하지 않는다.  
  - **각 서비스가 개별적으로 트랜잭션을 실행하면서 최종적으로 일관된 상태(Eventual Consistency)** 가 유지되도록 보장한다.
  - 따라서 중간 과정에서 일시적인 데이터 불일치가 발생할 수 있으며, 이를 해결하기 위한 보상 트랜잭션이 필요하다.

- **구현 방식**  
  1. **코레오그래피 기반 (Choreography)**  
     - **이벤트 기반 통신:** 각 서비스가 로컬 트랜잭션 완료 후 이벤트를 발행하여 다음 서비스가 이를 구독하고 실행한다.
     - **장점:** 중앙 조정자 없이 각 서비스가 독립적으로 트랜잭션을 처리하므로 결합도가 낮다.
     - **단점:** 전체 트랜잭션의 상태를 추적하기 어려울 수 있으며, 실패 시 보상 트랜잭션 관리가 복잡해질 수 있다.
  
  2. **오케스트레이션 기반 (Orchestration)**  
     - **중앙 오케스트레이터:** 하나의 중앙 관리자가 전체 트랜잭션의 흐름을 제어하고 각 단계의 실행을 명령한다.
     - **장점:** 전체 트랜잭션의 흐름과 에러 처리를 명확하게 제어할 수 있다.
     - **단점:** 오케스트레이터가 단일 실패 지점이 될 수 있어, 해당 컴포넌트의 장애가 전체 트랜잭션에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

### 5-4. 구현 전략
  - **동시성 제어:** 주문, 쿠폰 발급 등 공통 자원 접근에 Redis 분산 락 적용  
  - **분산 트랜잭션 관리:** 대부분의 서비스는 SAGA 패턴을 사용하여 로컬 트랜잭션 및 보상 트랜잭션 수행  
     - 강한 일관성이 필요한 경우 2PC 적용 검토 (단, 성능 저하 문제로 인해 최소화)  
     - MSA에서는 대부분 SAGA 패턴을 선호하며, 2PC는 최후의 수단으로 활용 

- **기대 효과:** 데이터 일관성, 확장성, 장애 격리 및 효율적인 실패 복구 확보

## 6. 분산 트랜잭션 제어 전략

### 6-1. 서비스별 로컬 트랜잭션
- **독립된 트랜잭션 관리:**  각 서비스(예: User, Point, Coupon, Product, Order, Payment)는 자체 데이터베이스와 트랜잭션을 사용해 내부 작업(생성, 조회, 수정 등)을 안전하게 처리한다.
  
- **실제 로직:** 서비스 내부에서 데이터 저장, 업데이트 등 모든 제어는 로컬 트랜잭션을 통해 이루어지며, 이를 통해 서비스별 데이터 정합성이 보장된다.

### 6.2 서비스 간 연동 및 이벤트 기반 통신
- **이벤트 발행 및 구독:** 한 서비스의 트랜잭션이 완료되면, 다음 작업을 위해 이벤트(또는 API 호출)를 발행한다.  
  예를 들어, 주문 생성 후 `OrderCreatedEvent`를 발행하면 결제 서비스가 이를 수신해 결제 처리를 시작한다.
  
- **분산 제어:** 각 서비스가 독자적으로 제어되는 로컬 트랜잭션과, 서비스 간 연동을 통한 보상 트랜잭션으로  분산 환경에서 데이터 정합성을 유지할 수 있도록 한다.

### 6.3 보상 트랜잭션 및 장애 대응
- **보상 트랜잭션(Compensating Transaction)**  
  분산 환경에서 중간 단계 실패가 발생하면, 이미 완료된 작업에 대해 보상 트랜잭션을 실행해 시스템 상태를 복구한다.  
  예를 들어, 결제 실패 시 주문 서비스에서 주문 취소 보상 로직을 수행한다.
  
- **동시성 및 장애 관리**  
  Redis와 같은 분산 락을 통해 동시 접근을 제어하며,  
  네트워크 장애나 타임아웃 상황에 대비해 재시도 로직 및 타임아웃 처리를 적용한다.


## 7. 결론
- MSA 전환을 통해 도메인별 독립성과 확장성을 확보할 수 있다. 
- 각 서비스는 개별 트랜잭션과 보상 트랜잭션으로 데이터를 관리해야 한다.  
- SAGA 패턴과 Redis 기반 분산 락을 활용해 분산 트랜잭션의 한계를 해결한다.

</details>




<details>
<summary>실시간 주문 데이터 전송의 이벤트 처리</summary>

## 변경사항
- 결제 완료 후 `OrderDataEvent` 이벤트를 발행하여, 결제 로직과 외부 데이터 전송 로직을 분리
- `event publisher`를 통해 주문 데이터를 비동기 이벤트로 발행
- `event listener`는 발행된 이벤트를 감지하여 외부 데이터 플랫폼으로 주문 데이터를 전송 - 34b0e0a

## 이벤트 퍼블리셔, 이벤트 리스너

### event publisher
  - 시스템 내에서 특정 시점에 이벤트 객체를 생성해 전달(발행)하여 작업이 필요한 컴포넌트들에게 트리거 역할을 수행한다.  
  - 이벤트를 직접적으로 호출하지 않고도 전달할 수 있어, 모듈 간 의존성을 줄이고 확장성을 높이는 장점이 있다.
  - 도메인 이벤트, 시스템 이벤트 등 다양한 상황에서 유연하게 적용할 수 있다.

### event listener
  - 발행된 이벤트를 감지하고, 해당 이벤트가 발생했을 때만 필요한 로직을 실행함으로써, 불필요한 호출을 최소화한다.  
  - 이벤트 기반으로 모듈을 분리할 수 있어, 기능 변경 또는 확장 시에도 다른 컴포넌트에 대한 영향이 적다.  
  - 비동기 처리와 결합하면, 트랜잭션 종료 후 별도의 흐름에서 로직을 실행하여 성능과 안정성을 높일 수 있다.
  - 이벤트 타입 매칭 : 발행된 이벤트 객체의 타입에 일치하는 모든 리스너 메서드들이 호출된다.


## 내 로직에서 이벤트 동작 방식

### event publisher
   - 결제 로직 내에서 결제 완료 시 `OrderDataEvent` 이벤트를 발행함
   - 이 이벤트는 현재 트랜잭션 내에서 생성되지만, 실제 처리는 트랜잭션 커밋 후 진행된다.

### event listener
   - `@TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)`를 사용하여 트랜잭션 커밋 이후 이벤트를 수신
   - `@Async` 어노테이션을 통해 비동기 방식으로 외부 데이터 전송 로직을 실행하여, 결제 트랜잭션에 영향을 주지 않음

## 요약
- 결제 트랜잭션 커밋 후에 비동기 프로세스로 이벤트가 처리되므로, 결제 로직과 외부 데이터 전송 로직이 서로 영향을 주지 않도록 변경하였다.

## 개선사항
- 현재 재시도 로직은 `@Retryable`이 최대 3번 재시도를 수행하지만, 최종 실패하면 `@Recover`에서 로그만 남기고 끝난다.
- 실패한 이벤트가 손실되지 않도록 Kafka, Redis Stream, DB 테이블 등을 활용하여 저장하고, 별도의 재처리 프로세스를 운영할 필요가 있다.

</details>


## PR 설명

body:
There were some questions if our implementation was correct and looking at the AMQP spec I see language supporting our approach. The mandated flow is:

> The drain flag indicates how the sender SHOULD behave when insufficient messages are available to consume the current link-credit. If set, the sender will (after sending all available messages) advance the delivery-count as much as possible, consuming all link-credit and send the flow state to the receiver. Only the receiver can independently modify this field. The sender's value is always the last known value indicated by the receiver.

- receiver sends a FLOW frame, with drain set.
- sender consumes all link credit as possible
- sender sends the flow state to the receiver

body:
This codemod hardens all [`readline()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.IOBase.readline) calls from file objects returned from an `open()` call, `StringIO` and `BytesIO` against denial of service attacks. A stream influenced by an attacker could keep providing bytes until the system runs out of memory, causing a crash.

Fixing it is straightforward by providing adding a size argument to any `readline()` calls.
The changes from this codemod look like this:

```diff
  file = open('some_file.txt')
- file.readline()
+ file.readline(5_000_000)
```

<details>
  <summary>More reading</summary>

 lookaside (that would _work_ if users set up lookaside).

Before this PR, _if the image had any non-sigstore signatures_, we would upload both the non-sigstore and sigstore signatures to lookaside.

@mheon @TomSweeneyRedHat PTAL. The bug has been that way for 2.5 years. I think the combination of required circumstances (an image must have both kinds of signatures, and the user must have configured lookaside, not use of sigstore tags, while somehow requiring sigstore signatures) makes it unlikely that users would rely on it, but I can’t quite rule it out.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
## Remediation

This change fixes "Log Injection" (id = [log-injection](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/java/java-log-injection/)) identified by CodeQL.

## Details

This change ensures that log messages can't contain newline characters, leaving you vulnerable to Log Forging / Log Injection.

If malicious users can get newline characters into a log message, they can inject and forge new log entries that look like they came from the server, and trick log analysis tools, administrators, and more. This leads to vulnerabilities like Log Injection, Log Forging, and more attacks from there.

Our change simply strips out newline characters from log messages, ensuring that they can't be used to forge new log entries.
```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Newlines;
  ...
  String orderId = getUserOrderId();
- log.info("User order ID: " + orderId);
+ log.info("User order ID: " + Newlines.stripNewlines(orderId));
```

<details>

  * [https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Log_Injection](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Log_Injection)

Created using the documentation at [Inflection AI for Developers](https://developers.inflection.ai/). You can obtain an INFLECTION_API_KEY from there by registering.

Their API currently supports streaming.

Their API does not yet support: image, file, tool-calling, JSON mode, or OpenAI API compatibility, but when does features arrive support could be added.

I am not affiliated with Inflection AI, I'm just adding support so others can take advantage of the work I put into making their API compatible with the AI SDK.

author: bencurran98
body:
# Fix inconsistency in writestring due to unicode encoding

## Description
This fixes a bug that crops up sometimes when reading VLRs and EVLRs from a LAS file whose descriptions contain unicode characters with 2 bytes of length instead of 1. Basically, when we write a VLR description, we call `writestring(io, description, 32)` (since as per the LAS spec, the description should be 32 bytes in length). However, `writestring` would add a buffer to the string (trailing "\0" 's) if **`length(description)`** is < 32, even if `size(description) == 32`, meaning we're adding extra bytes to the file causing some corruptions down the line. 
This turns into a simple fix, just replacing `length` with `size` in `writestring`

## Types of Changes

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

body:
#### PR Classification
New feature to enhance model selection in the chat application.

#### PR Summary
This pull request introduces a new endpoint for retrieving available models and updates the chat service to support model selection during chat streaming. Key changes include:
- `ChatController.cs`: Added `GetModelsAsync` endpoint to fetch available models.
- `ChatService.cs`: Implemented `GetModelsAsync` method and adjusted chat streaming logic to use the selected model ID.
- `ChatStreamRequestDto.cs`: Introduced `ModelId` property to specify the model for chat streaming.
- `ModelDto.cs`: Created a new DTO to represent model information.
- `prompt-box.component.html`: Added a dropdown for model selection, populated from the store service.

## Description

Closes https://github.com/stacks-network/sbtc/issues/1323

## Changes

* Implement `WithdrawalRequestReport::validate`.
* Add new withdrawal request constants that are consensus critical for validation. They are
  * `WITHDRAWAL_BLOCKS_EXPIRY`, which is the value suggested in https://github.com/stacks-network/sbtc/issues/620,
  * `WITHDRAWAL_BLOCKS_WAIT`, which is from the last paragraph of the opening comment of https://github.com/stacks-network/sbtc/discussions/12 and in the comments of https://github.com/stacks-network/sbtc/issues/16, 
  * `WITHDRAWAL_DUST_LIMIT` which is the max dust amount for a standard transaction using the default `dustrelayfee` config setting from bitcoin core.

This PR adds a unit test for each of the different `WithdrawalValidationResult`s variants.

body:
Improve the implementation of `picoquic_probe_new_path_ex` to incorporate tests and return detailed error codes.

Add API `picoquic_subscribe_new_path_allowed` to either return immediately if `picoquic_probe_new_path_ex` is expected to succeed, or program the stack to execute a callback `picoquic_callback_next_path_allowed` when the next call to  `picoquic_probe_new_path_ex` is expected to succeed.

Use these two API in `picoquicdemo` to provide an example.

This should address issue #1835

author: shellspeed1
body:
## About The Pull Request

Persistence is supposed to be a cybersun front but it still uses interdyne comms. Lets fix that and add interdyne comms as an emergency comms chip.

Additionally, this PR disables the icemoon automapper as we have been having consistent issues with missing roofs. This is hopefully a temporary fix until a better solution can be found. 

Lastly, reworks engineering a bit to add one more construction spot and make the utilities room a bit easier to notice so water actually gets set up. Also expands table space in the kitchen as that was one of the more desired features.

## Why It's Good For The Game

I love not having holes in the roof. Also flavor on the comms as we are supposed to be a cybersun front.

## Proof Of Testing

<details><summary>Screen caps from testing</summary>
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a110e756-5ae5-4ddf-b5b2-f2bb56af29d5)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36c4e595-c182-45ad-851c-64de760e988c)
</details>

## Changelog
:cl:
add: Persistence now has cybersun comms (It's literally just renamed persistence comms)
add: Persistence can now produce interdyne comms in an emergency using an interdyne comms chips
fix: Persistence no longer has 4 safes on one tile
fix: Persistence no longer has a turret that shoots out a window in the prison
fix: Persistence no longer has a null telecomms server, also atmos works
fix: Renamed syndicate_exofab to syndicate exofab in the circuit printer
fix: Renamed cybersun channel no longer outputs to the uplink channel
fix: Reverts automapper placement of persistence on icemoon and returns to 
map: slightly revamped the Persistence kitchen.
map: condensed the utility area of persistence and added a cycling airlock plus one more 3x3 construction area.
map: toned down some of the roundstart persistence equipment that can be acquired through other relatively easy means such as cargo. 
/:cl:

This pull request includes several changes to the `ProcessEvaluation` job, database migrations, and various Python scripts for bubble detection and configuration. author: stsuruno-openai
body:
# Situation

- When two responses are generated by the model in a short time, the second response is sometimes not played back in audio 
- This happens when the first response is long. While the first response is being played back, the second response is generated. The `output_audio_buffer` is created only for the first response and not for the second response.
- In this repo, I encountered the error in the `customerServiceRetail` scenario. When I am transferred from the `authentication` agent to the `return` agent, I could hear the line from the former but not the latter

# Proposed solution

- Wait to send a client event `response.create` or to transfer agents in function calls until all output_audio_buffers are cleared. Responses will not be created until all preceding responses are played back.

author: khluu
body:
1. Load some models from S3 path with `runai-model-streamer` instead of HF by default (only a few test jobs so far, listed below)
2. Add `runai-model-streamer` and `...-s3` into CI dependencies
3. Allow to pull more files from S3 than just `*config.json`
4. Strip `/` from file path when determining destination file path so it doesn't default to `/...` which machine doesn't have access to write into
5. Add `/` into model S3 path if there's no `/` at the end, mainly to prevent cases where 2 models on S3 bucket match the pattern and confuse the model loader
6. Don't look for files in HF repo if the model starts with `/`, which means the model path is a S3 path and model name is already converted to S3Model().dir which looks like `/tmp/tmp3123..`

Test jobs with models loaded with S3 (not all test files, just as many as I can):
- Entrypoints llm/ (I haven't done so for `openai/` ones yet since they are set up with the remote server and the S3 model path somehow messed things up) 
- Basic correctness
- Basic models
- Metrics & Tracing 
- Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker Test

Package name: @mantine/carousel
  • 7.16.1 - 2025-01-19

    What's Changed

    • [@ mantine/core] Menu: Add withInitialFocusPlaceholder prop support
    • [@ mantine/core] Slider: Fix onChangeEnd being called when disabled prop is set
    • [@ mantine/core] Add option to customize chevron color with chevronColor prop in Select and MultiSelect components
    • [@ mantine/core] Fix incorrect styles of nested tables (#7354)
    • [@ mantine/core]: NumberInput: Fix onChange being called in onBlur if the value has not been changed (#7383)
    • [@ mantine/core] Menu: Add data-disabled prop handling to Menu.Item component (#7377)
    • [@ mantine/form] Fix incorrect values handling in form.resetDirty (#7373)
    • [@ mantine/chart] AreaChart: Fix gridColor and textColor props being passed as attributes to the DOM node (#7378)
    • [@ mantine/hooks] use-in-viewport: Fix tracking being stopped when used with a dnd library (#7359)
    • [@ mantine/core] MantineProvider: Fix jest tests not running in case there is incorrect window.matchMedia polyfill implementation (#7360)
    • [@ mantine/core] Modal: Fix Escape key not working in old Safari versions (#7358)

    New Contributors

    • @ kidonng made their first contribution in #7364
    • @ Benjaminsson made their first contribution in #7360
    • @ cameronrdecker made their first contribution in #7380
    • @ tomrehnstrom made their first contribution in #7373

author: denik
body:
## Changes

diff.py is like "diff -r -U2" but it applies replacements first to the argument.

This allows comparing different output files and directories but ignore differences that are going to be replaced by placeholders.

This is useful for tests that record large amount of files, specifically "bundle init" with standard templates. In those tests, changing one parameter results in a small diff so recording the full directory is not helpful, because it's hard to see what changed there. I'm using it in implementation of serverless mode for templates that need it: #2348 The serverless templates are slightly different from classic, capturing the diff helps to see exactly where.

Related small changes:
- Add [TESTROOT] replacement for absolute path to acceptance directory in git repo.
- Add $TESTDIR env var for absolute path to a given test in git repo.

## Tests
- New test acceptance/selftest/diff to test the helper.
- Via #2348 which makes use of this feature.

I've not been able to find an authoritative static site generator for Lua, so am suggesting something I've been using for several years that I just published. Works with Lua 5.1-5.4, requires no other dependencies. Unlike most such tools, this doesn't take on additional dependencies to support markdown. Instead I build my website https://akkartik.name using raw HTML.

If one is willing to edit HTML, what can an SSG provide? The answers I've come up with so far are:
* Giving pages on a site a shared look and feel using a minimal template.
* Stitching pages together into index pages with pagination.
* Autogenerating RSS and [HTML Journal](https://journal.miso.town) feeds so readers can be notified of new posts.

This tool provides one 150 line script for each of these concerns. Each script can be used independently of the others. For example I generate two sets of index pages on my site.

author: hansedong
body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to CoreDNS!
Please provide the following information to help us make the most of your pull request:
-->

### 1. Why is this pull request needed and what does it do?

Currently, the implementation of the NS function in `plugin/backend_lookup.go` of CoreDNS is as follows:

```go
func NS(ctx context.Context, b ServiceBackend, zone string, state request.Request, opt Options) (records, extra []dns.RR, err error) {
    // NS record for this zone live in a special place, ns.dns.<zone>. Fake our lookup.
    // only a tad bit fishy...
    old := state.QName()

    state.Clear()
    state.Req.Question[0].Name = dnsutil.Join("ns.dns.", zone)
    services, err := b.Services(ctx, state, false, opt)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    // ... and reset
    state.Req.Question[0].Name = old

    seen := map[string]bool{}

    for _, serv := range services {
        what, ip := serv.HostType()
        switch what {
        case dns.TypeCNAME:
            return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("NS record must be an IP address: %s", serv.Host)

        case dns.TypeA, dns.TypeAAAA:
            serv.Host = msg.Domain(serv.Key)
            ns := serv.NewNS(state.QName())
            extra = append(extra, newAddress(serv, ns.Ns, ip, what))
            if _, ok := seen[ns.Ns]; ok {
                continue
            }
            seen[ns.Ns] = true
            records = append(records, ns)
        }
    }
    return records, extra, nil
}
```

In `plugin.NS`, when `Services()` returns an error, the function returns directly without resetting the query name back to original. This leaves the query name set to the internal lookup value ("ns.dns.<zone>") in error cases.

So, in this case, the DNS domain name has actually been changed, not the original value. And when the caller of `plugin.NS` (possibly a plugin) needs to pass the request to the next plugin for processing, the domain name processed by the next plugin is not actually the origin domain name.

This PR ensures the query name is always reset to original value before error handling, making the error path consistent with the success path.

Before:

```go
if err != nil {
    return nil, nil, err  // Query name remains as "ns.dns.<zone>"
}
// ... and reset
state.Req.Question[0].Name = old
```

After:

```go
// Always reset the query name to original first
state.Req.Question[0].Name = old
if err != nil {
    return nil, nil, err  // Query name is properly reset
}
```

### 2. Which issues (if any) are related?

None

### 3. Which documentation changes (if any) need to be made?

No

### 4. Does this introduce a backward incompatible change or deprecation?

No

- [ ] Tutorials - R tutorials for how to use certain packages and tools (usually code is embedded)

author: akshay20t
body:
## Why are these changes needed?
With existing AutoGen implementation of Bedrock client class `BedrockClient`, the Amazon Bedrock inference request gets timed out when the input token size is large (>~10,000 tokens). This happens because the current implementation uses default read and connection timeout values (60 seconds) from `boto3` while initializing the `Config` class. Due to this default value the `create` method in `BedrockClient` class raises `RuntimeError` even though bedrock model is still generating response (as monitored in AWS CloudWatch).

With increasing context window size of LLM in today's Generative AI era, it is important to introduce capability for user-defined read timeouts to support large input tokens for agents.


## Related issue number
Closes #5505

This PR changes the way fields are redacted using raw json.  It previously started with the list of sensitive fields and tried to find the json path based on that.  However this didn't work for arrays of complex objects.

Now the code starts with all the JsonPaths, and then looks up the sensitive fields list.  One thing to note is that before it looks up the sensitive fields list, it removes the array element from the path.

author: gjeanmart
body:
# [Part 4 - Close #325] [Processor API] [Feat] Handle Challenge - Finalize & Execute Settlement

## Overview

This PR implements the final step of the challenge process after a settlement is either **proven correct** (`SettlementProven`) or **invalidated** (`SettlementInvalidated`).

It is **Part 4** of a multi-step integration plan for **#325**:

1. **#371**
   - Listen for `SafenetSettlementEngine.SettlementChallenged(settlementHash)`.
   - Record the challenge in the system.

2. **#372**
   - Call `SafenetEntryPoint.sendAttestation(attestationHash)` (Spend Chain) after challenge detection.
   - Listen for `SafenetAttestationRecorded(attestationHash)` (Home Chain).

3. **#374**
   - Call `SafenetProtocolGuarantees.prove(attestationHandle, data)` and `SafenetAttestationHandler.bridgeVerificationReceipt(attestation)` (Home Chain).
   - Listen for `SafenetProtocolGuarantees.ProtocolGuaranteeProven(attestationHash)` events.

4. **#376** _(This PR)_
   - Listen for `SettlementEngine.SettlementProven(settlementHash)` events (Debit Chain).
   - Listen for `SettlementEngine.SettlementInvalidated(settlementHash)` events (Debit Chain).
   - Trigger settlement execution.

---

## Changelog

### Processor Service

#### 🔹 Persistence Module
- **`ChallengePersistence`**: Updated `updateStatus(id)` to `updateStatus(chainId, settlementHash)` for better compatibility.
- **`SettlementPersistence`**: Added methods `markAsProven` and `markAsFailed` to update debit status.
- **`TransactionPersistence`**: Ensured debits are always ordered by `debit.index` to prevent flaky tests.
- **`SafenetTransactionDebitEntity`**: Introduced a new status `PROVEN`.

#### 🔹 Settlement Module
- **`SettlementEventsListener`**:
  - Added listeners for `SettlementEngine.SettlementProven(attestationHash)` and `SettlementEngine.SettlementInvalidated(attestationHash)` events.
- **`SettlementScheduler`**:
  - Updated SQL queries to find settlements with:
    - `status = INITIATED` and challenge period expired.
    - `status = PROVEN`.
- **`SettlementService`**:
  - Reacts to `SettlementProven` by updating the debit status to `PROVEN` and marking the challenge as `INVALID`.
  - Reacts to `SettlementInvalidated` by updating the debit status to `FAILED` and marking the challenge as `VALID`.

#### 🛠 Misc
- Updated documentation and diagrams

author: perfaram
body:
This PR implements [RFC 3030](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3030), which defines the CHUNKING and BINARYMIME extensions. 

This implementation is rather conservative in the changes it makes to gen_smtp, in particular regarding the API. 

On the server side, **by default**: 
* CHUNKING is enabled, as it is possible to fully abstract away how a message was delivered, from the PoV of a user of this library;
* BINARYMIME is disabled (unless activated in the `handle_EHLO` callback by setting it to `true`) because such messages always bypass the newline fixing and may not be UTF8, contrary to what one might reasonably expect when implementing `handle_DATA`. It is not currently possible to know whether a message was sent with this body type, should this be implemented? Feedback welcome here.

On the client side, **by default**: 
* CHUNKING (i.e., the `BDAT` command) will not be used, even if possible, **for now** (I'd like to have feedback first, but otherwise it should not be a problem to use it by default whenever possible);
* BINARYMIME will not be used, unless enabled through the options (so, session-wide -- I think it might make sense to allow setting this per-email? Feedback welcome here).

author: kickster97
body:
### WHAT is this pull request doing?

The mqtt.default exchange cannot be created with a regular `Exchange::Declare` frame, we create it in the `Broker` class and inject it into the `vhost.exchanges`. We have been creating these exchanges as durable, meaning they are written to the defintions file. 
This causes issues when we load definitions.
This PR makes the MQTT exchange non-durable, so it will not be stored in definitions and in turn not cause these exceptions.

author: pdesoyres-cc
body:
When we build the components for testing integration inside the console, we don't want the full prepack process to be executed (tests, lint, documentation, etc.)

This PR splits the prepack script into 2 sub npm scripts:
* The dev mode runs only the `components:build`
* The prod mode runs the full build and code quality checking

The prepack step will check for the `DEV` env var to run one or the other mode.

body:
## Related issues

#180 

## Changes

This PR adds a standalone crate under `/crates/storage-pricing` for doing all the necessary calculations for:
- the operational cost of storing _n_ bytes of data
- network fees for storing data that the user has to pay
- EMA for the Irys token price (denominated in USD) that are to be stored in the block headers (storing this data will be added in a future PR)
- piggybacking extra lints that have been added to the root Cargo.toml 🙈 

This PR **does not** add any functionality to the node itself. 

## Linter

All linter checks pass for `cargo clippy -p storage-pricing`

author: m-fila
body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Use the same event and run type in `UniqueIDGenSvc` as in `edm4hep::EventHeader`. Add generating id directly from `edm4hep::EventHeader`. **This changes the ID values !**

ENDRELEASENOTES

Calling `getUniqueID` with arguments taken from `edm4hep::EventHeader` is the most common usage of that function. Until https://github.com/key4hep/EDM4hep/pull/398 the function arguments and `EventHeader` had different signedness.
After that PR they have the same signedness but different widths, with the function arguments being shorter - which means there is a huge range of valid `EventHeaders` that will get the same ID due to an implicit cast

I propose to deduct the correct types from `EventHeader` as in #278 and #279. I also propose to add an overload taking `EventHeader` directly since this is the most common usage and avoids a possible issue with manually assigning wrong type.

**This changes the ID values !**

author: joelwurtz
body:
This PR replace https://github.com/HFQR/xitca-web/pull/1176

A different approach is used here

Mainly we try to read 1 byte from the stream in a sync way, since we didn't send anything yet we should receive a WouldBlock io error, if we doesn't receive this it either means : 

 * the stream is in a different error so it should be closed
 * the stream has some data left and then is in an incorrect state so we should close it
 * the stream has been closed (so we should closed it also)

Retrying here should be safer since we don't consume request, i still use a middleware so user will opt in for this feature

I only handled the h1 connection closed error here, we could add other cases later when request could be retried safely in those cases

Implements:

- Basic functionality to refer to content on github and gitlab to include in your book

- [x] Add cleaning up `_git` dir to clean up routine
- [x] Merge files from external repo to main book files;
  - [x] requirements.txt so plugins are available
  - [x] _config.yml so the plugins actually work

- [x] Check licenses of external books to avoid biggest copyright issues
- [x] CI tests
- [x] Documentation

ToDos:

- Automagically add headers in the built pages that properly acknowledge where they came from
- #60

<hr>

_How to test_

- Add an external file to the ToC of one of your books, e.g.;
```yaml
    - external: https://gitlab.tudelft.nl/interactivetextbooks-citg/risk-and-reliability/-/blob/v0.1/book/intro.md
```
- Run `teachbooks build`

_Notes_

- config.yml and references.txt are **not** merged automatically as resolving duplicates/conflicts there is very challenging. The user is warned upon building the book which plugins and dependencies are in external content but not in the main book
- references.bib file is updated to include any references of external content

author: wauplin
body:
In this PR:
- Adds an autouse function-scoped fixture that overwrites the default HF_HOME with a temporary directory for each single test => all tests are made independent + it won't mess-up with local cache at all anymore. Let's check it doesn't break anything in CI.
- Sets the tokens for inference tests to `HF_INFERENCE_TEST_TOKEN` instead of `HF_TOKEN`. The problem of `HF_TOKEN` is that it is overwritten in `pyproject.toml` to `""`, making it ineffective. To update VCR tests locally, one has to manually edit `pyproject.toml` which is annoying.
  - => in practice, VCR tests seem to be skipped in CI because no token is set => this is independent from this PR and @hanouticelina is working on it (right?)
- Removes deprecated `_old_token_path`. Used only internally and deprecated since Nov. 2022 https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/issues/1232

author: asterized
body:
Uwuification does not work well, especially for shorter strings of text, as too little effects like tildes and emojis are added (examples given below). This PR increases the amount of tildes, as well as bump certain amounts of parameters in the case of short strings to further optimize uwuification.

Examples:
Before:
```py
>>> import imsosorry
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! how awe you doing?'
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! h-how awe you d-doing?'
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! how awe you d-doing?'
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! h-how awe y-you doing?'
```

After:
```py
>>> import imsosorry
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo~ ^^;;  how a-awe you doing?'
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! h-how a-awe~ you doing~ (✿oωo) '
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo! how awe you doing?'
>>> imsosorry.uwuify("hello! how are you doing?")
'hewwo~ 😳😳😳  how awe~ you~ d-doing?'
```

Notice a large difference in the quality of uwuified text before and after.

body:
### Summary
In #18487 the `attributeValues` of objects were made into a immutable object of type `AttributeValues` which internally is essentially a map of attribute IDs as keys and the respective value. This meant that `attributeValues.attribute` no longer is a valid reference in the API. In DHIS2-18970 we look into ways to allow using properties of the attributes of attribute values as filters. 

For the Gist API this is a new feature as they never supported filtering on attribute properties for the attribute values of the list entity type. However, it is easier to add this in Gist API as it is for the metadata API. 

In this PR 2 filter features are added:
* filtering by attribute values for a attribute of a certain ID, `filter=attributeValues.attribute.id:eq:<uid>` is automatically converted to the equivalent filter `filter=<uid>:!null` where the attribute ID is used as a property (which was an existing feature)
* filters that target properties of the attribute via the attribute values are now supported and translate to special SQL, for example, `filter=attributeValues.attribute.name:like:foo`. As always in Gist API these are limited to persisted properties of the attribute.

### Automatic Testing
New tests were added for the added filter functions.

### Manual Testing
* SL demo DB
* check `/api/organisationUnits/gist?fields=name,id,attributeValues&filter=attributeValues.attribute.id:eq:ihn1wb9eho8` has matches
* check `/api/organisationUnits/gist?fields=name,id,attributeValues&filter=attributeValues.attribute.name:like:KE` has matches

# Description

No existing issue, just something Rust Analyzer does that I thought would be nice to have.

## Summary

(it's better to review this commit by commit as the first one just moves things around)

Now hovering over an integer literal will show its inferred type together with its decimal value and hexadecimal value (Rust Analyzer also shows the binary (`0b...`) literal but I omitted that because Noir doesn't have such literals).

  - Added functions to analyze video for suspicious activities using OpenVINO face detection and head pose estimation models (`analyze_video`).
  - Added functionality to extract audio from video files and transcribe it using Deepgram's API (`extract_audio_from_video`, `transcribe_audio`, `analyze_audio`).

* **Question Generation:**
  - Implemented a new function to generate interview questions based on a resume PDF and job description using the Gemini AI model (`generate_questions`).

### Frontend Integrations:

* **App Routing:**
  - Added routes for new interview-related pages (`/interview`, `/interview-result`) and integrated them into the main layout (`client/src/App.tsx`).

* **Profile Page Updates:**
  - Enhanced the `Profile` component to display different document sections based on the user's role (student, admin, HR) (`client/src/pages/Profile.tsx`).

* **Interview Page:**
  - Created a new `Interview` component to handle the AI video interview process, including video recording, question display, and uploading the recording for analysis (`client/src/pages/admin/Interview.tsx`).

author: iainsproat
body:
## Description & motivation

Express middleware we use may handle errors incorrectly. For example, external middleware may create errors which are not compatible with `BaseError`. Or we may have been inconsistent in catching errors.

This can cause issues when recording error metrics & logs, or can cause Express to suspend the request without logging or metrics.

In this PR we aim to provide a consistent means of handling errors from middleware and routes, ensuring they are correctly recorded in metrics & logs. We also aim to prevent unexpected behaviour from Express by handling errors in a manner it expects.

## Changes:

- Introduces a wrapper function / boilerplate to be wrapped around every Express request handler as so:

    ```
    handleErrors({
        handler: (req, res, next) => { /* actual request handle here */ },
        verbPhraseForErrorMessage: 'doing some request handling',
        defaultErrorType: MyRequestHandlerError
      })
    ```

## Description
In our image refs ( e.g. `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0.200-alpine3.21` ), Renovate is able to patch the first part (e.g. `9.0.200` -> `9.0.201`), but it does not support patches to the last part (e.g. `alpine3.21` -> `alpine3.22`.

This PRs extends this repo's renovate config to support patches of alpine OS image tags. The solution is pasted from [this article](https://aarongoldenthal.com/posts/managing-alpine-linux-based-container-images-with-renovate/), which describes a situation similar to ours.
Here is a regex playground where you can see how this manager will target the dependency details: https://regex101.com/r/qcgvRM/2

author: macdue
body:
When SVE is available use the `-sve` variant of memcpy from AOR for `__arm_sc_memcpy`. From: https://github.com/ARM-software/optimized-routines/blob/71e36403858ab3ff743fcde336fb31890e57af7e/string/aarch64/memcpy-sve.S

This implementation uses FPR/ZPR load/store instructions to do the copy, so should not cause memory hazards if called in streaming mode (with the memory later being accessed in the streaming mode with SVE/SME instructions).

The implementation has been slightly modified from AOR to use local labels (matching other compiler-rt functions) but still passes the memcpy and memmove tests from AOR.

author: henrystivens
body:
This pull request involves several updates to our MySQL database schema, admin interface navigation, accessibility enhancements, and codebase cleanup. Key highlights include:

1. **Renaming the MySQL Schema:** The existing `ku_admin` schema has been renamed to `koot`. This reorganization includes changes to schema and table names, as well as adjustments to primary keys, unique indexes, and foreign key constraints to align with the new schema name.

2. **Updating Admin Navigation Links:** Trailingslash usage in navigation links was added for consistent routing and resource loading. The "Roles" link has been removed due to redundancy or removal based on current functionality.

3. **Improving Accessibility:** Aria-label attributes have been added to navigation elements to enhance accessibility, improving usability for users with disabilities.

4. **Removing Unused Create Views:** The unused create views for resources and users were removed from the codebase. These views are no longer necessary and are being deleted to maintain a cleaner project structure.

5. **Improving Scaffold Creation and Editing:** A refactoring has been performed to switch to using `ModelLiteForm` for creating HTML forms based on model metadata. This new class simplifies controller logic, provides more flexible form generation, and ensures data persistence in case of validation failure with necessary HTML escaping for security.

These changes aim at enhancing the structure, maintainability, accessibility, and performance of our application.

author: darkgnotic
body:
Using the (wire + AST) `protocolVersion` in the Permissions protocol will be too sensitive. For the percentage of users that don't bother to wait for server deployments to complete before deploying new permissions (e.g. zbugs), this will unnecessarily result in errors every time we change the wire-protocol.

Because the Permissions only relies on the AST schema, consider the data "supported" if it (strictly) parses with its valita schema. This means that semantic changes must be accompanied by a change in the AST format, which unsupporting code will correctly fail to parse. This should pretty much always be the case; we just have to never, e.g. change the meaning of an existing field or something like that.

  * AE
  * DS
  * HF
  * BSR

  * build
  * lint
  * ci
  * docs
  * feat
  * fix
  * perf
  * refactor
  * test
  * chore
  * dbt

body:
In soft floating-point ABI, this function takes the double argument as a pair of registers r0 and r1.

The ordering of these two registers follow the endianness rules, therefore the register on which the bit flipping must happen depends on the endianness.

### What changed? Why?

This PR helps expose some more staking related details:

1. `fee recipient_address` and `forwarded_fee_recipient_address` on validator
2. `pending_claimable_balance` on external address via the staking context api

### Testing

1. Fee recipient address being populated on validator

```
> const coinbase = Coinbase.configureFromJson({ filePath: "~/code/cb/staking/.coinbase_cloud_api_key_production.json" });
undefined
> let ea = new ExternalAddress("ethereum-mainnet", "0x7F639032a6D973044b27F90A522b5b4d81466906");
> let validators = await Validator.list("ethereum-mainnet", "eth", ValidatorStatus.ACTIVE);
> let v = validators[0];
> v.getFeeRecipientAddress()
'0x7f639032a6d973044b27f90a522b5b4d81466906'
> v.getForwardedFeeRecipientAddress();
''
```

2. Pending claimable balance avaialble via context balance api

```
> const coinbase = Coinbase.configureFromJson({ filePath: "~/code/cb/staking/.coinbase_cloud_api_key_production.json" });
undefined
> let ea1 = new ExternalAddress("ethereum-mainnet", "0xc2c3382BD01bc629a35FC3b452841A2b86Ca8F33");
undefined
> await ea1.stakeableBalance("eth", StakeOptionsMode.PARTIAL, {"integrator_contract_address": "0xc4dcb059dd98b45b090da8982234c61d0b9e84f9"});
0.028164762175712832
> await ea1.unstakeableBalance("eth", StakeOptionsMode.PARTIAL, {"integrator_contract_address": "0xc4dcb059dd98b45b090da8982234c61d0b9e84f9"});
0.007584138538653242
> await ea1.claimableBalance("eth", StakeOptionsMode.PARTIAL, {"integrator_contract_address": "0xc4dcb059dd98b45b090da8982234c61d0b9e84f9"});
0
> await ea1.pendingClaimableBalance("eth", StakeOptionsMode.PARTIAL, {"integrator_contract_address": "0xc4dcb059dd98b45b090da8982234c61d0b9e84f9"});
0.000099999999999998
>
```

body:
## Problem

The test is flaky: WAL in remote storage appears to be corrupted. One of hypotheses so far is that corruption is the result of local fs implementation being non atomic, and safekeepers may concurrently PUT the same segment. That's dubious though because by looking at local_fs impl I'd expect then early EOF on segment read rather then observed zeros in test failures, but other directions seem even less probable.

## Summary of changes

Let's add s3 backend as well and see if it is also flaky. Also add some more logging around segments uploads.

ref https://github.com/neondatabase/neon/issues/10761

author: xabg2
body:
This PR refactors the way mocks are created and utilized in test cases. Previously, mocks were defined as constant variables, which limited flexibility and could lead to unintended state persistence across multiple tests.

With this update, mocks are now encapsulated within functions, ensuring that each test case receives a fresh and isolated mock instance when needed. This approach enhances test reliability, reduces potential side effects, and improves maintainability by providing greater control over mock initialization.

By implementing this change, we improve test consistency and make the mocking strategy more scalable for future test expansions.

author: jamesjieranshen
body:
Some structural changes to the core Rat executable. Previously pre-event-loop configuration are scattered between the ctor and in the Begin() method. This is all moved to a dedicated Configure() method, called by the Begin() method prior to the main event loop. This allows downstream experiment to override this method in a more flexible way than before. Concretely, this solves the issue that downstream processors do not have access to the ratdb tables.

Note that this change is effectively trivial -- `tools/rat.cpp` calls the constructor and Begin() method back-to-back. The only complexity comes from how the rat class is extended in downstream experiments like EosSimulations.

body:
# Flashlight & Creature PR
Please make sure the Wire Box Puzzle PR is reviewed and merged first to check for conflicts in that order (should be fine?)
## Flashlight
- **Shoulder-Mounted Lights Prefab**: manages flashlight(s) on shoulders
  - should just be placed within PlayerCapsule (currently)
  - I didn't apply adding this to the prefab for worries about conflicts since we are all touching the prefab but its drag-and-drop into the player prefab with no configuration needed
- **Controls** for toggling lights: "F" and right-mouse button both work as defaults
  - toggles lights
  - toggles creature stun trigger
- **FlashlightCharge**: stored as public static variable in GameManager (not part of saved data)
  - charge decreases over time while on
  - inspector variable for max charge duration
- **Turning Delay**: 
  - lights follow camera in gradual motion
  - inspector variable to tune light turning sharpness

## Creature
- Singleton **CreatureManager**
  - tracks player, manages current speed, and aggro & stun logic
  - when not in aggro (i.e. player in light) speed decreases at twice the rate it ramped
- **Creature Zone** Prefab
  - detects player entry into creature zone and spawns/despawns the creature through CreatureManager
  - creature is spawned at FURTHEST spawn location option to prevent spawning on top of player when coming from certain angles
  - Only works if its corresponding light is UNPOWERED (for any reason: light switch, busted box, zone off, etc.)
  - this is the thing we will be dragging into scenes when building levels
  - Individual Customization: zone collider (can be any collider type), corresponding PoweredLight, & list of spawn locations
  - _Note_: zones should overlap somewhat to prevent player from bouncing between zones to constantly reset creature to stall it awkwardly
    - creature will only respawn in new zone once player has actually fully left previous zone
- **Creature** Prefab
  - Does nothing unless player is within a certain range to activate aggro
  - Rotation lerps to face player (lerp speed scales with speed increases)
  - Moves only in its forward direction with ramping speed, with a variable slow-down multiplier when not directly facing player
  - Aggro & speed carries when creature respawns in newly entered zone
    - only fully loses instant-aggro (regardless of distance) once its speed reaches back to 0
  - no need to ever put this in scenes - all handled through Creature Zone prefab
- **Creature Stunning**
  - If powered flashlight is ever aimed at creature, it stuns for 1.5 seconds, then regains normal behavior and cannot be stunned again until after a 4.5 second cooldown (numbers subject to change)
    - if you all would prefer, I sort of also like the idea that we could slightly increase the stun time if its only a max one-time stun per aggro rather than cooldown
  - instantly stuns off cooldown if light was already shining at creature

## Misc.
- PowerSystem no longer requires manually assigning of individual elements per zone
  - it just fetches children on Awake instead - only a one time costly operation

The original code had a significant command injection vulnerability in the following line:
```java
String cmd = "/usr/games/cowsay '" + input + "'";
```
This allowed an attacker to inject arbitrary commands by manipulating the 'input' parameter. The vulnerability has been addressed by changing the command execution to:
```java
processBuilder.command("bash", "-c", "/usr/games/cowsay", input);
```
This approach separates the command and its arguments, preventing command injection. However, it's important to note that while this change significantly reduces the risk, it may not completely eliminate it. Additional input validation and sanitization should be considered for maximum security.

Another security improvement is the replacement of System.out.println with proper logging:
```java
private static final Logger LOGGER = Logger.getLogger(Cowsay.class.getName());
LOGGER.info(cmd);
```
This change enhances the application's ability to monitor and track operations, which is crucial for security auditing and troubleshooting.

Lastly, the error handling has been improved:
```java
LOGGER.log(Level.SEVERE, "Error running cowsay command", e);
```
This change ensures that exceptions are properly logged, aiding in debugging and preventing sensitive information from being exposed to end-users.

author: cratelyn
body:
this commit introduces a new method to `tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<T>`.

broadly speaking, users of the oneshot channel are encouraged to `.await` the `Receiver<T>` directly, as it will only yield a single value.

users implementing their own `std::future::Future`s directly may instead poll the receiver via `<Receiver<T> as Future<Output = Result<T, RecvError>::poll(..)`. note that the contract of `Future::poll()` states that clients should not poll a future after it has yielded `Poll::Ready(value)`.

this commit provides a way to inspect the state of a receiver, to avoid violating the contact of `Future::poll(..)`, or requiring that a oneshot channel users track this state themselves externally via mechanisms like `futures::future::FusedFuture`, or wrapping the receiver in an `Option<T>`.

NB: this makes a small behavioral change to the implementation of `<Receiver<T> as Future<Output = Result<T, RecvError>::poll(..)`. this change is acceptable, per the `Future::poll()` documentation regarding panics:

> Once a future has completed (returned Ready from poll), calling its
poll method again may panic, block forever, or cause other kinds of problems; the Future trait places no requirements on the effects of such a call.

the upside of this is that it means a broken or closed channel, e.g. when the sender is dropped, will settle as "finished" after it yields an error.

see:
* https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/7137#discussion_r1940242052
* https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/future/trait.Future.html#panics

author: dmcavoy
body:
Robots.txt files are very important for Search Engine Optimization. They make help robots find the right pages on our site to crawl and index. 

This PR suggests adding /projects/ routes to the disallow list in the robots.txt file which means bots trying to crawl the site should not look at any page with a /projects/ route. 

I'm proposing this change for a couple reasons:
- We should not have student projects showing up in search results. 
- These pages are some of the pages on our site marked as "poor performance" in the Google Search Console. [Example ](https://search.google.com/search-console/core-web-vitals/drilldown?resource_id=sc-domain%3Acode.org&item_key=CAMQARgD)

## Summary and Scope

* Bump cray-kyverno from 1.6.6 to 1.7.0 to pull in changes that remove pod security policies in preparation for the move to K8s 1.32.

## Issues and Related PRs

* Resolves [CASMPET-7328](https://jira-pro.it.hpe.com:8443/browse/CASMPET-7328).
* Fixed by cray-hpe/cray-kyverno#38.

## Testing

### Tested on:

  * `molly` (K8s 1.32)

### Test description:

I pulled the 1.7.0 `cray-kyverno` Helm chart and ran a manual upgrade on `molly`. The Helm upgrade completed successfully; all of the expected workloads were running, and matched what's running on beau, which has an existing 1.6.6 `cray-kyverno` deployment.

## Risks and Mitigations

Risk is fairly low, since the bulk of the chart changes involve removing pod security policy resources, along with RBAC resources that facilitate using PSPs. There was one modification to a role that involved removing PSP permissions but keeping the existing role, but the expected workloads were all healthy, so we can assume that that modification didn't break anything.

author: arthurstomp
body:
This PR fixes the remainig failing test in CI.

The `encode` function creates its 2x bytes output by merging 2 vectors of x bytes intercalating the values by if the index is even or odd. However, in the `decode` function splits the same 2 x bytes vector by just cutting it in half. That difference in strategy on splitting those larger vector seems to be the cause of the failing test.

This PR adds  new function `nibble_chunk` that splits a larger vector in 2 smaller vectors using the even/odd strategy from the `encode` function.

body:
Zooms in and Out the screen.

`The syntax always comes in pairs. The first parameter of each pair indicates whether you are using a direct value or a variable/indirect variable, through ValueOrVariable().`

------------------------

#### Syntax (TPC):
```js
@raw 2059,
      "",          // Not Used.
      0, 0,        // Scale value in percentage (Default is 100%).
      0, 1,        // Origin Type (0 = absolute pixel || 1 =percentage of screen area )
      0, 50,        // Origin X
      0, 50,        // Origin Y
```

#### Example:
```js
@raw 2059, "", 1, 20, 0, 0, 1, 21, 1, 22 // size is var20, absolute pixel, originX is var21, originY is var22
```

-----------------------------------

This command differs from maniacs patch zoom, which is executed per picture layer, and it has a interpolation between zoom states and a "wait for completion" check.

body:
`jj split --parallel` now sets the working copy revision (`@`) to the first revision created by the split instead of the second. As a result, `@` remains on the same change id before and after the split.

There is no good reason to choose the second commit as the working copy commit after a --parallel split. The only reason it works that way today is because doing that didn't require any code changes compared to the non parallel split.

Martin proposed this change in the review for https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/pull/5618.

body:
# Image rotation

## Description
This PR adds the rotation feature by saving/updating the `Orientation` exif tag to a sidecar file. Afterwards, it queues jobs to regenerate thumbnails, which now use the saved orientation value. The only thing left to do is change the url so it can bypass the frontend cache which currently relies on `asset.checksum`, which isn't updated with this type of edit. 

## API Changes
```
PUT /api/assets { assetIds: [], orientation: <1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8> }
PUT /api/assets/:id { orientation: <1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8> }
```

Fixes #8355 (and potentially double rotates other HEIF images, which can at least now be fixed in the web ui directly)

author: joao-pedro-p-holanda
body:
This pull request fixes a problem when a string value is given to the `scopes` parameter in the `Security` class. Currently, the parameter `scopes` is expected to be a `Sequence[str]`, but python strings fit both the types `str` and `Sequence[str]`, causing every character to be treated as different string, and consequently scope.

e.g.
```python

app = FastAPI()

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl="token",
    scopes={"me": "Read information about the current user.", "items": "Read items."},
)


def my_auth_function(security_scopes: SecurityScopes, token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)]):
    return security_scopes.scopes


@app.get("/me")
async def read_single_scope(
    current_scope: Annotated[list[str], Security(my_auth_function, scopes="me")], 
    # type checkers won't give an alert or error in scopes because a str is also a Sequence[str]
):
    return {"scopes": current_scope}
```

Requesting in `/me` with the `Authorization` header set to _"Bearer \<any_text\>"_ would show the scopes as ['m','e'], because the string is treated like a sequence of single characters.

Related: #13368

body:
# Ya es posible crear registros en la base de datos
### User Story 1: Crear un Registro
#### Como usuario, quiero poder agregar nuevos nombres a la base de datos, para que pueda almacenarlos y acceder a ellos en el futuro.

#### Criterios de aceptación:

- [x] El sistema debe permitir al usuario ingresar un nombre.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8045ba5c-146a-4e9b-b56f-6ea31af007d3)

- [x] El nombre ingresado debe ser guardado en un archivo de texto o en memoria (si se usa almacenamiento temporal).
- [x] El nombre debe ser almacenado junto con un identificador único (ID).
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd2360ed-0732-45af-937d-21006279d986)

> [!NOTE]  
> - El nombre ingresado **se guarda junto a su ID en un archivo**, y además, **se guarda el último ID del último registro en otro archivo, para facilitar la obtención del último ID registrado, sin necesidad de manipular el archivo donde están los nombres directamente,** ya que este sufre modificaciones constantemente y si se eliminan registros o se agregan nuevos, puede ser que se pierda la información acerca de cuál fue el último ID registrado, o también puede que se dificulte el cálculo u obtención del mismo.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b340b2b-2d8b-42ac-ab3e-de2f276c0ad7)

> [!NOTE]  
> - **Si el usuario no le pasa como argumento el nombre que quiere para la base de datos** al programa, **el programa le asigna el nombre "`nombres.db`" a la base de datos** y al archivo que contiene el último ID el asigna el nombre de  "`nombres.db.inf`" (solamente le agrega la extensión ".inf" al nombre de la base de datos)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b340b2b-2d8b-42ac-ab3e-de2f276c0ad7)

> [!NOTE]  
> - Si el usuario le pasa al programa el nombre que quiere para la base de datos, el programa le asigna ese nombre a la base de datos y para el archivo que contiene el último ID, toma el nombre de la base de datos y solamente le agrega la extensión ".inf"
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e19f0b7-bdc7-4dd1-8b2c-6bdbae314d3f)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee45d5d6-f161-46d2-9548-cfd1e4d285ff)
Closes  #3

body: #### Summary This fixes some console warnings that are printed to the console when working on the web app. They only appeared in dev mode For the first one, I don't think the error had any effect since I'm pretty confident that the only reason it caused an error was because of a Babel plugin that was adding `propTypes` to something that it thought was a component. author: winner245
body:
This PR refactors `basic_string` a bit to simplify its implementation in the following ways:
- Instead of manually checking whether a string is short or long, followed by calling the specific functions (e.g., `__get_short_size()`, `__get_long_size()`), we call the general functions (`size()`) to hide the conditional checks and make the code more concise.
- Once a string is determined to be short or long, we directly call the specific functions instead of the general versions to get rid of unnecessary internal conditional checks. For example, for a long string, we would directly call `{__set, __get}_long_pointer` instead of `{__set, __get}_pointer()`. 
- Variables that are defined in both the `if` and `else` branches are now declared in a common scope to reduce redundancy.
- When the string size is calculated multiple times using `traits_type::length(__s)`, a variable is introduced to store its length. While modern compilers can optimize this with constant folding, explicitly storing the length improves code readability and makes the logic clearer.
- Fixed synopsis with missing default arguments.

author: tomjohn1028
body:
### Change notes
* New top-level environment variable/CLI arg
   * SAVE_PATH: renaming of `META_MERKLE_TREE_DIR`. Path where all generated operator files are stored
* Separates each stage of the process into more coherent functions. 
    * `run` CLI command loops through each stage, saving the outputs to _save-path_ CLI argument. The output from each stage is held in memory to reduce the processing.
        * New Environment Variables/CLI Args for `run`
           * STARTING_STAGE: Ability to start the operator from a specific stage before it continues
             * one of: `load-bank-from-snapshot, create-stake-meta, create-merkle-tree-collection, create-meta-merkle-tree, cast-vote, wait-for-next-epoch`  
           * SAVE_STAGES: true/false - whether to save the state of intermediate stages in files. Needed for CLAIM_TIPS and SET_MERKLE_ROOT
           * SAVE_SNAPSHOTS: true/false - whether to save the bank loaded in the target as a full snapshot (~100GB).
* Create CLI commands for each stage
    * _snapshot-slot_ - Create and store a full snapshot for a given slot
    * _create-stake-meta_ - For a given epoch and slot, load the bank and create the `StakeMetaCollection` file which contains validator vote accounts and their staking delegations.
    * _create-merkle-tree-collection_ - For a given epoch, load the `StakeMetaCollection` from disk at _save-path_, generate and save the `GeneratedMerkleTreeCollection`.
    * _create-meta-merkle-tree_ - For a given epoch, load the `GeneratedMerkleTreeCollection` from disk at _save-path_, generate and save the`MetaMerkleTree`.
    * _submit-epoch_ - For a given epoch, load the MetaMerkle file and cast a vote to the NCN's ballot box. Optionally set the merkle root on the Tip Distribution account if the NCN has consensus for the epoch.
    * _claim-tips_ - For a given epoch, generate and execute Tip Distribution Claim instructions for any unclaimed tips.
* TipRouter saved files
    * generated files are now saved under _save-path_
    * Files _<= current_epoch - num_monitored_epochs_ are purged for anything
    * NOTE: file names have change to a _{epoch}_file_name.json_ format. All previous files will not be removed. Operators should manually delete old files.
